headline: Venmo vs Cash App vs Zelle fees
description: Compare Venmo Business, Cash App Business, and Zelle fees for freelancers—including instant transfer costs, $100 examples, and when each P2P rail makes sense.

itemListElement.name: Venmo vs Cash App vs Zelle fees

acceptedAnswer.text: It is usually $0 for eligible transfers at participating banks, but banks can set their own disclosures. Confirm on Zelle’s help center and your bank’s fee schedule. Free does not mean protected like a merchant payment.

mainEntity.name: Which is cheaper for a $100 business payment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zelle is usually $0. Between business profiles, Venmo Business (~$2.00 on $100) typically beats Cash App Business (~$2.75 at 2.6% + $0.15) on this snapshot—before instant cash-out fees. Verify live rates in the calculators.

mainEntity.name: Do instant transfers change the winner?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can. Venmo instant ~1.75% and Cash App instant ~1.5% apply on top of payment fees when you cash out immediately. If you always use instant, include both layers in reverse pricing.

mainEntity.name: Can I use personal Venmo for freelancing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial activity generally belongs on business profiles/products. Personal rails may lack appropriate protections and can conflict with platform policies. Prefer business profiles or full merchant processors for client work.

mainEntity.name: When should I refuse P2P entirely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Refuse when the buyer is unknown, the deliverable is reversible digital goods with high dispute risk, or the client pushes for personal payments to avoid business fees. Use Stripe or PayPal Goods & Services instead.
